title: Studying the Effects of Task Diversity Using Small Mathematical Worlds
abstract: arXiv:2610.13750v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Basic mathematical tasks like modular addition have been a valuable tool for illuminating aspects of neural network behavior that are challenging to see in noisy, unverifiable, large-scale, real-world settings. These studies have typically focused on a single task. However, modern language models are exposed to a vast number of tasks despite being trained with a next-token prediction objective. In this work, we introduce two mathematical task ecosystems, IntWorld and PermWorld, built from distinct but related tasks on integers and permutations. Both are designed to simulate task diversity within a cohesive mathematical 'world' where tasks are distinct but related. Because the datasets are procedurally generated, we can precisely vary the number of tasks, allowing us to begin to disentangle the role of task variety from other factors in training. translated_title: 使用小型数学世界研究任务多样性的影响
translated_abstract: 摘要：像模加法这样的基础数学任务一直是揭示神经网络行为某些方面的宝贵工具，而这些行为在嘈杂、不可验证、大规模的现实世界环境中往往难以观察。以往这些研究通常只聚焦于单一任务。然而，现代语言模型尽管仅通过下一个词预测目标进行训练，却接触到大量不同的任务。在这项工作中，我们引入了两个数学任务生态系统——IntWorld和PermWorld，它们由整数和排列上彼此不同但相互关联的任务构建而成。两者都被设计用于在一个内聚的数学“世界”中模拟任务多样性。由于数据集是程序化生成的，我们可以精确地改变任务的数量，从而开始将任务多样性的作用与训练中的其他因素区分开来。在描述了这些数据集之后，我们提供了从这些数据集中获得的一些初步结果。
tldr: 本文提出了两个程序化生成的数学任务生态系统IntWorld和PermWorld，通过精确控制任务数量，实现了对任务多样性如何影响神经网络训练的系统研究。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces two procedurally generated mathematical task ecosystems, IntWorld and PermWorld, enabling systematic study of how task diversity affects neural network training by precisely varying the number of tasks.
